findings.desc: overflow_auto bypasses its documented visible-approval guard: core/lattice-dispatch starts the dispatch when either approve=true or start=true is present, so --start=true alone materializes dispatch state even though the CLI/docs promise suggest-only behavior unless visibly approved. This breaks the manual-first user-visible contract for overflow_auto.

[HIGH] packages/main/src/core/lattice-dispatch.ts:845 and 1054-1066 leave approved real-host dispatch_run/overflow_auto without a usable overflow worktree. prepareDispatch writes only metadata and explicitly leaves worktree creation undone, but the scaffolded real-host run path tells the operator to run codex/claude/gemini in .worktrees/overflow/... anyway. Repro: node packages/main/dist/cli.js --root <tmp> lattice dispatch run --storyId=B-real --host=codex --json returned status=needs_receipt with nextAction pointing at .worktrees/overflow/B-real/D-B-real-codex-..., while the recorded dispatch.json showed worktreeExists=false for that path. That breaks the required host-overflow workflow in docs/requirements/decisions/host-overflow.md:52-54, where Lattice must project an isolated overflow worktree before the host works in it, so the approved real-host overflow path cannot actually execute.
